area_summary:
Every menu and full-screen UI scene in this area draws its J2DScreen through the painter's one J2DOrthoGraph, `dComIfGp_getCurrentGrafPort()->setPort(); scrn->draw(0,0,graf)`. That graf is set up in mDoGph_Painter (m_Do_graphic.cpp:1572-1573 and :1890; `bl J2DOrthoGraph::setOrtho` 0x802CDD14 at 0x8000B06C and 0x8000BA30). So the 2D agent's global compression reaches every one of these screens for free, and none of them needs its own transform hook. That covers item, collect, dmap, fmap/fmap2, save, option, file select, name entry, file error, title (REL actor), opening, game over and auction. The compression must be done by widening the ortho box, not by narrowing the GX viewport. The reasons: J2D's own clip scissor follows the ortho (J2DOrthoGraph::scissorBounds), and the full-screen capture blits, both cloth draws and the list2D J3D models all assume the viewport stays 640 wide. The painter ortho is -9..659, so its centre is game x=325, not 320. At 16:9 the visible game range becomes 325±334F (-120..770), and the edge-anchor shift is 334(F-1) game units (80 EFB px).

What is left falls into three groups.
(1) Full-screen leaf pictures: black dim masks (msk0/blak/.msk/wts1/mask) and cloth backdrops (..cl, ms01/ms02, HK00/HK01). After compression they would cover only the centre. One T2 hook on the only call to `J2DScreen::set(stream)`, the `bl` at 0x802D09DC, widens them at load (Rule A, about 0x150-0x200 bytes). A tag list in the same hook stretches the black edge bars (save iris wp04-07, opening mak1/mak2) out to the real edges (Rule B). Every menu calls scrn->set() before fopMsgM_setPaneData, so the Orig values are captured already widened and all per-frame paneTrans/scale/alpha code stays consistent. All of Gecko's 60000000 NOPs in this area are alpha writes on exactly these masks; Gecko hides the masks, while Rules A/B widen them. The opening and game over `li r4,0` patches draw those screens uncompressed and stretched; we don't need them.
(2) The two 3D cloths, which use viewport W/H × g_HIO.mAspectRatio, and the file-select camera. These depend on which aspect knob the 3D agent picks. Under the g_HIO knob the pause/sea-chart cloth needs a uniform scale-up (data only). Under the 4/3-literal knob the file-select camera and cloth need two hooks instead.
(3) Cosmetic leftovers: slide-in notes, the title ship and the opening panorama show a little earlier in the side bands. Optional edge-anchoring: auction price counter, file-select button cluster.

Cheap (shared): graf inheritance (free), Rule A + Rule B (one T2 hook, about 0x200 bytes), capture blits (free). Moderately expensive and knob-dependent: the cloth and file-select camera, 2 data words or 2 hooks. Everything for title, opening, file select, name entry and file error runs before Link exists and before the REL's 300-frame gate, so it must live in T2 or be a patcher-side DOL patch. Pause menu, game over and auction could call into the REL, but the hook sites belong to core T2. Acceptable as 'centred 4:3 with full-width backdrop' after Rules A/B: item, collect, dmap, sea chart, save, option, file select, name entry, file error, title, opening (pillarboxed on black), game over, auction. None of these screens needs per-pane relayout to be correct. Real per-site work: the cloth (DEFAULT/CLOTH_ONLY scale, or the file-select pair), plus a live check of the save iris wipe.

items.assumption: The graf ortho is -9..659 x -21..524 mapped onto a 640x480 viewport. The screens assume that 2D box is the whole display.
items.effect_native: Without the global compression, every menu is stretched ×F. With it, every menu is correct but confined to the centre 4:3. That is the intended baseline for this area.
items.anchor: centre (the compression is about EFB centre = game x 325, the centre of -9..659)
items.fix: No per-screen work. HARD CONSTRAINT for the 2D agent: compress by widening the ortho box (left = 325-334F, right = 325+334F, or the equivalent), not by narrowing GXSetViewport. Reasons: J2DOrthoGraph::scissorBounds (J2DOrthoGraph.cpp:47-56) scales by mBounds.width/mOrtho.width, so auction's setScissor(true) clipping follows. The capture blits (d_menu_capture.inc:47, d_gameover.cpp:44) draw a 0..1 quad against the viewport. Both cloth draws use viewport W/H. The list2D J3D models (title ship/subtitle) use the current projection. Express any edge-anchor shift in this area as (-9 - new_ortho_left) = 334(F-1) game units, taken from the 2D hook's constant, never a hard-coded 320(F-1).
items.gecko: Gecko widens the 2D globally another way and patches per screen. Its `li r4,0` patches (0x80234528 opening, 0x8018F5CC gameover) pass a NULL graf so J2DScreen::draw builds its own J2DOrthoGraph(0,0,640,480) (J2DScreen.cpp:155), i.e. that screen is drawn uncompressed and stretched.
items.live_check: With the 2D hook active, open each screen. All panes should sit undistorted in the centre 4:3, and the backdrops should be dealt with by the items below.

items.effect_native: With the compression alone the masks dim only the centre 4:3. Side bands stay bright during note pop-ups (item/collect/dmap), the options screen, the save prompt and the game-over fade. The sea chart's opaque cloth (..cl) and the treasure-chart cloths (ms02) cover only the centre, so the 3D menu cloth or capture shows in the bands.
items.fix: T2 core hook: proj.hook_branchlink("j2d_screen_set_hook", 0x802D09DC). The C body does: ok = J2DScreen_set_stream(scr, stream); if (ok && ws_mode()==2) walk(scr, 0, 0); return ok. walk(pane, ax, ay) iterates the children. For each child c: cx0 = ax + c.x0, cy0 = ay + c.y0, cx1 = ax + c.x1, cy1 = ay + c.y1. Rule A applies if mMagic=='PIC1' && c.childCount(+0xB8)==0 && cx0<=0 && cx1>=640 && cy0<=0 && cy1>=480. Then set x0' = 325-(325-cx0)*F - ax and x1' = 325+(cx1-325)*F - ax, and call J2DPane::setBasePosition(c, c->m2DBasePosition) (0x802D0800) to refresh the pivot and matrix. Recurse into children with (cx0, cy0). Do NOT touch PAN1 containers (ROOT is 640x480 and moving it would shift every child). This must run in T2, because title, opening, file select and file error load before Link and the REL gate. About 0x150-0x200 bytes. Ordering makes it safe: every menu calls scrn->set() before fopMsgM_setPaneData, which copies Orig from the pane (f_op_msg_mng.cpp:9814-9828), so later fopMsgM_paneTrans/ScaleXY/alpha calls (fmap paneTransBase on mClPane, d_menu_fmap.cpp:2263) use the widened Orig. Limitation: it acts at load. Menus reload every open; title/file-select/HUD screens keep the old width until their next load after a mode change. The same hook also matches screens outside this area: wipe_01_01 ..b1/..b2, operate_wind_mask 'mask', hukidashi BACK (textureless). One shared site; other agents must not add a second. Optional extension, the same mechanism as a per-file anchor table: stash the file name with hook_branchlink at 0x802D0968 (`bl 0x802B68F0` JKRFileLoader::getGlbResource, r3 = name), then apply {file, tag, L/R shift} entries in the same walk (see menus-auction, menus-fileselect-2d).

items.effect_native: Save iris: the black frame stops short of the real edges, leaving bright bands left and right of the vignette. Opening: the letterbox bars are 4:3 wide. That is invisible over the black clear colour (g_clearColor 0x803F61A0 = 00000000), but wrong if anything is drawn behind.
items.anchor: full_width (each edge that touches 0 or 640 is pushed to the real edge; the inner edge is kept)
items.fix: In the same T2 walk: if the pane tag is in {'wp04','wp05','wp06','wp07','mak1','mak2'} (u32 multi-char) and it is a childless PIC1. If cx0 <= 0, set x0' = 325-(325-cx0)*F - ax. If cx1 >= 640, set x1' = 325+(cx1-325)*F - ax. Then call setBasePosition(c, c->m2DBasePosition). The texture can't be checked cheaply at runtime, hence the tag list; 'no2k'/'no3k' black note shadows in wipe_01_01 show why a texture rule is unsafe. The same tags are black edge bars in d_scope (wipe_00 wp04-07, d_scope.cpp:120-123) and the picture box (wipe_00_2, d_picture_box.cpp:119), so the rule is right there too. The HUD agent may add sp04/sp06/.ct1/.ct2/wp01-04 for wipe_01_01. PaneScaleAlphaWipe recomputes wp04 x = wp02.w+wp01.w (left edge stays at the iris, the widened width extends right) and wp05 x = -wp05.w (extends left), using the widened mSizeOrig. wp06/wp07's formula -(wp00.w + wp05.w) could not be reconciled with the .blo offsets, hence medium confidence. Fallback if the live check shows gaps: do what Gecko did and keep the wipe's alpha constant (NOP the `bl fopMsgM_setNowAlpha` at 0x801DAA38, a patcher-side DOL patch) or force its alpha to 0.
items.gecko: Gecko NOPs the setNowAlpha in PaneScaleAlphaWipe's loop (0x801DAA38), so the iris never fades. It does nothing for mak1/mak2: it draws the whole opening uncompressed via `li r4,0` at 0x80234528.
items.live_check: Pause → Quest Status → Save (openForCollect): watch the iris vignette close and check the four corners and both side bands for unblackened gaps. Also game over → Continue (gameContinue3). Opening: new file → watch the story pictures for bars reaching both edges (only visible if the clear colour is changed).

items.effect_native: If the 3D knob is g_HIO.mAspectRatio (the culling plan's choice), the cloth frustum widens by F and the mesh no longer covers. At 16:9 the corner radius needed is 3286 against 2670, so the frozen capture shows at the band corners/edges, varying with the random rotation. items.fix: Only under the g_HIO knob. Primary (data only, no code): the mode-2 setter, ws_init or the WS_SET op handler in T2, writes a uniform scale = base × k(F) to BOTH x and y of DEFAULT (0x803E5EC0/C4, base 1.78) and CLOTH_ONLY (0x803E5F70/74, base 1.7), where k(F) = sqrt((2126.5F)² + 1661.3²)/2698.6 (16:9 → 1.218, i.e. 2.168/2.071; 21:9 → ≈1.53). Restore 1.78/1.7 on leaving mode 2. It takes effect at the next menu open (cloth_init copies it). X-only scaling would not work because DEFAULT rotates randomly. Do NOT scale FILE_SELECT (type 1, hard-coded at d_menu_cloth.cpp:229). Fallback (stretch instead of enlarge): hook_branchlink at 0x801DFA04 with a C function that calls C_MTXPerspective(mtx, f1, f2 / F, f3, f4). Also T2 core, about 0x30 bytes.

open_questions: Knob choice (3D agent): under g_HIO.mAspectRatio (0x803B9A08) the file-select camera and cloth widen for free, but the pause/sea-chart cloth needs the l_HIO uniform scale (0x803E5EC0/C4, 0x803E5F70/74). Under the 4/3 literal (0x803FA998) the pause cloth is free, but the file select needs hooks at 0x8023003C and 0x802324A8. Pick one and tell this area which branch to build.

2D agent: confirm the compression widens the painter's ortho (setOrtho calls 0x8000B06C/0x8000BA30) rather than the GX viewport. The capture blits (d_menu_capture.inc:47, d_gameover.cpp:44), both cloth draws (viewport W/H) and the list2D models depend on the viewport staying 640. Also publish the ortho's new left edge so per-screen anchor shifts use (-9 - new_left) and not 320(F-1). The painter's centre is game x 325.

Save iris wipe (PaneScaleAlphaWipe, d_menu_save.cpp:1750-1797): the decomp places wp06/wp07 at x = -(wp00.w + wp05.w), which does not match their .blo offsets (-78). Rule B's edge extension for wp04-wp07 needs a live look (Quest Status → Save). The fallback is Gecko's alpha NOP at 0x801DAA38.

Rules A/B live in one shared T2 hook at 0x802D09DC. The HUD/textbox agents should add their tags (scope/picture-box wp04-07 already match; wipe_01_01 sp04/sp06/.ct1/.ct2/wp01-04; operate_wind_mask 'mask' is already Rule A) to the same table instead of adding a second hook. Budget about 0x200 bytes of T2 against the 0xBF8 free (minus the culling hook).

Load-time widening uses the factor at screen load. Title, file-select and HUD screens loaded before a mode/aspect change keep the old width until their next load. Menus reload on every open. Acceptable, or should the WS_SET op force a re-walk of resident screens?

Pause cloth coverage numbers are geometric (mesh at depth 6200, fov 30°, waves ignored). Confirm k(F)=1.218 at 16:9 live across several random rotations; the sea-chart CLOTH_ONLY cloth (scale 1.7) has the least margin.

The title (d_a_title) is a REL actor. I assumed attr().field_0x0C (the ship's entry and exit distance) only puts the ship off-screen and nothing else; verify live that nothing on the title depends on x outside 0..640.
